## Two pattern formats

**Simple format**: matches a tool name or a Bash command.

```json
"permissions": {
  "allow": ["Bash(git *)", "Bash(pnpm *)", "Read", "Edit"],
  "deny":  ["Bash(rm -rf *)", "Bash(sudo *)", "Bash(npm publish)"]
}
```

**Path patterns**: Read, Edit and Write accept the path pattern directly. Do not add `file_path:`; that qualifier is invalid for these tools.

```json
"permissions": {
  "deny": [
    "Read(*.env*)",
    "Edit(*.pem)",
    "Write(*.key)",
    "Read(*credentials*)"
  ]
}
```

## Glob syntax

| Pattern | What matches |
|---------|--------------|
| `Bash(git *)` | Any git command |
| `Bash(npm test*)` | `npm test`, `npm test:watch` |
| `Read(*.env*)` | `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.prod` |
| `Edit(./src/**)` | All files under `src/` |
| `Write(*.key)` | Any `.key` file |

## Progressive levels

```json
// Level 1 - Auto-approve read tools
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"] } }

// Level 2 - Git + package manager
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob",
    "Bash(git *)", "Bash(pnpm *)"] } }

// Level 3 - Full development
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob",
    "Edit", "Write", "Bash(git *)", "Bash(pnpm *)"] } }
```

## Behavior of the three categories

| Category | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `allow` | Auto-approved, no prompt |
| `deny` | Completely blocked |
| `ask` | Confirmation requested |
| (default) | Default permission mode |

## Known limitation

A path rule restricts matching tool access; it cannot remove a secret already pasted into a prompt or returned by another tool. Keep sensitive data outside the process access boundary and review shell, MCP and sandbox controls together.

## Where to define permissions

```
~/.claude/settings.json       (global, all projects)
.claude/settings.json         (project, shared with team)
.claude/settings.local.json   (local machine, gitignore)
```

**Rule evaluation**: deny rules from any scope take precedence over ask and allow rules. A local allow cannot override a managed or user-level deny. Use local settings for project-specific preferences within those limits.
